A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, added, and removed material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention measurements, ImageNet classification experiments, aggregation ablations, and COCO detection and instance-segmentation results.

after.justification: v2 reports original attention measurements and classification experiments, including additional low-shot, fine-grained, attentive-probing, and object-localization results.

M1.justification: The linear scorer, softmax weighting, and weighted pooling of frozen representations remain. Beyond renaming this approach Selective Aggregation, v2 adds an explicit variant aggregating the [cls] token together with patch tokens (Section 5 and Table 1).

E1.justification: v2 adds CUB-200 fine-grained classification and ImageNet object localization while retaining ImageNet classification. It removes v1's COCO object-detection and instance-segmentation evaluation (Appendix B.3), substantially revising task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated CAPI and DINO-v2 encoders and removes the supervised ViT comparator, which also disappears from the corresponding attention plots. Appendix C.2 adds comparisons against one-head and twelve-head Attentive Probing; the earlier SA-AbMILP and non-trainable aggregation comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The original full-ImageNet probing protocol remains. v2 adds an ImageNet-1% label-budget condition and specifies SGD with batch size 1024 for it and CUB, introduces attention-head controls and MaxBoxAccV2 localization evaluation, and explicitly permits a DINO-v2 pretraining-data exception. The COCO Mask R-CNN evaluation protocol is removed.

E4.justification: v2 adds the [cls]-inclusion ablation, the one-versus-twelve-head Attentive Probing analysis, and localization case studies. It removes the COCO analysis of classification fine-tuning's effects on dense prediction. Existing scorer-design ablations, alternative aggregation analyses, and the KLD comparison are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three random seeds, without confidence intervals or formal significance tests. v2 relocates the seed statement from Section 5.1 to Appendix B.2; the added results do not establish a changed statistical reporting practice or increased run count.

E6.justification: v2 adds classification, probing, localization, and [cls]-inclusive aggregation results while removing COCO results and supervised-comparator series. For example, new CUB results report MAE-B accuracy of 45.8 with standard representations and 65.9 with Selective Aggregation. Most shared Table 1 values remain, but DINO's patch-only aggregation accuracy changes from 74.7 to 75.2.

T1.justification: The aggregation sum and softmax normalization extend from patch indices 1 through N to indices 0 through N for the [cls]-inclusive variant. v2 also corrects the classifier parameter count from D(K+1) to (D+1)K. The ViT, MAE, and Shannon-entropy mathematics otherwise remain; moving the entropy definition to the appendix adds no theory.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes diagnosing ineffective aggregation and presents AbMILP as a proof of concept. v2 explicitly presents Selective Aggregation as a practical method contribution. The central claims about MIM's aggregation deficiency and improvements without encoder fine-tuning remain.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the convergence-based explanation of increased MAE [cls] self-attention after fine-tuning with an attention-redistribution hypothesis. It adds the interpretation that Attentive Probing benefits may arise from multiple aggregation patterns, while removing the COCO-supported warning about classification versus dense-prediction tradeoffs. The general checkpoint-coverage limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies that BEiT-v2 excludes intermediate ImageNet-21k fine-tuning and documents settings for the new SGD and attention-head experiments. COCO detector implementation information is removed. The original ImageNet hyperparameters, four-GH200 hardware disclosure, and code address remain; v1's appendix already described the code as available.

R1.justification: v2 develops a substantial positioning argument distinguishing representation-preserving aggregation from attentive probes that transform features, supported by new discussion and evaluation of Attentive Probing. It adds recent MIM and localization references, including CAPI and MIM-refiner. Much of the earlier general SSL discussion is retained in Appendix A rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial portions of Sections 4–6 are rewritten around Selective Aggregation. Attention findings are reorganized, detailed methodology moves to the appendix, broader related work becomes Appendix A, and overhead receives a separate subsection.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a full-width explanation combining attention maps, semantic-object attention, and an aggregation diagram. Table 1 gains an aggregation column, new evaluation tables and localization illustrations appear, and supervised curves are removed with corresponding axis and legend changes. The earlier aggregation-map gallery is retained as renumbered Figure 9.

improvement.justification: The new CUB and low-label evaluations strengthen evidence for practical applicability, while the controlled Attentive Probing comparison clarifies the contribution of aggregation. The redesigned overview also improves explanation. Removing the COCO study and its dense-prediction caveat loses useful evidence about applicability boundaries, tempering the overall improvement.
